title: Worth Doing and Other -ing Expressions
summary: Judge whether an action is useful or worthwhile with no point in, no use, no good and worth + -ing. Describe difficulties, time spent or wasted, busy activities, and common go + -ing activities.
learningObjectives: Explain why an activity is pointless using there is no point in, it is no use and it is no good with -ing.
Recommend or reject activities with worth + -ing, including worth it and nouns followed by worth + -ing.
Describe how easily an action happened using have trouble, difficulty or a problem + -ing.
Use spend/waste time + -ing, be busy + -ing, and go + -ing naturally in relevant contexts.

explanation.heading: Say an effort will not help: no point in, no use and no good
explanation.body: Use there is no point in + -ing when an activity has no practical purpose or benefit. It is no use + -ing and it is no good + -ing make a similar judgement, often because the activity will not improve the situation. The usual patterns differ: no point in includes in, whereas no use and no good go directly before the -ing form. Ask “What is the point of + -ing?” when questioning the purpose of an action. The past form there was no point in is also common.
explanation.example: There is no point in restarting the printer while the electricity is off.

explanation.heading: Recommend worthwhile actions with worth
explanation.body: Use be worth + -ing to say an activity rewards the time, money or effort it takes: the course is worth taking; the question is worth discussing. Negative forms include not worth + -ing. If the activity has already been mentioned, use worth it or not worth it instead. With an object, retain any needed preposition: a speaker worth listening to.
explanation.example: The extra rehearsal was tiring, but it was worth it.

explanation.heading: Talk about difficulty or the absence of it
explanation.body: Use have difficulty + -ing, have trouble + -ing and have a problem + -ing to describe an action that is hard to complete. Change have to had when reporting the past; add no or any to discuss an easy task: had no difficulty understanding and did not have any trouble finding. Difficulty with -ing is more standard here than difficulty to do.
explanation.example: Our visitors had no trouble locating the workshop from the directions.

explanation.heading: Describe time and current work
explanation.body: Use spend + a period of time + -ing when describing how time is used. Waste + time + -ing suggests that the activity was unproductive. Be busy + -ing explains what occupies someone, often giving a reason they cannot do something else. These patterns use -ing rather than a to-infinitive after the time expression or busy.
explanation.example: The volunteers spent the afternoon sorting donations for the shelter.

explanation.heading: Use go + -ing for recreational activities
explanation.body: We commonly use go + -ing to name outings, sports and leisure activities, including go swimming, go hiking, go climbing, go camping and go shopping. Change go to goes, went or have gone as the context requires, but keep the activity in -ing. This is a familiar activity pattern, not a rule that every verb after go takes -ing.
explanation.example: We went paddleboarding on the river during our holiday.

comparisons.title: A pointless effort versus a worthwhile one

left.label: There is no point in + -ing
left.example: There is no point in waiting outside; the office is closed.
left.note: The speaker expects no benefit from continuing the action.

right.label: Be worth + -ing
right.example: The online talk is worth attending even after a long day.
right.note: The speaker judges that the action brings enough benefit to justify the effort.

left.label: Spend time + -ing
left.example: Ellie spent an hour updating the map.
left.note: Spend reports how time was used without necessarily judging it.

right.label: Waste time + -ing
right.example: Ellie wasted an hour searching an outdated directory.
right.note: Waste explicitly evaluates the time as unproductively used.

examples.sentence: It is no use printing another copy when the ink cartridge is empty.
examples.note: No use is followed directly by -ing and highlights a futile action.

examples.sentence: The small gallery is worth exploring, even if you have only twenty minutes.
examples.note: Worth + -ing recommends an activity as rewarding.

examples.sentence: The new receptionist had difficulty remembering all the room numbers.
examples.note: Have difficulty is followed by the -ing form.

examples.sentence: The designer is busy preparing mock-ups for tomorrow’s review.
examples.note: Busy + -ing names the activity occupying the designer.

examples.sentence: They have gone snorkelling near the reef for the afternoon.
examples.note: Have gone + an -ing activity indicates that they are away doing it.

commonMistakes.incorrect: That history podcast is worth to listen to.
commonMistakes.correct: That history podcast is worth listening to.
commonMistakes.why: After worth, use -ing; keep the final preposition required by listen to.

commonMistakes.incorrect: There is no point in to send the form again.
commonMistakes.correct: There is no point in sending the form again.
commonMistakes.why: The preposition in takes an -ing verb, not to + verb.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The visitors had difficulty to find the entrance.
commonMistakes.correct: The visitors had difficulty finding the entrance.
commonMistakes.why: Use an -ing form after have difficulty when naming the challenging activity.

commonMistakes.incorrect: We went to hiking in the national park.
commonMistakes.correct: We went hiking in the national park.
commonMistakes.why: The common leisure-activity construction is go + -ing, without to.

studyTips: Ask whether the effort can change the outcome; choose no point in or no use when it cannot, and worth + -ing when it can pay off.
Learn short chunks rather than individual words: had no trouble finding, spent an hour revising, and was busy organising.
Plan three realistic leisure outings using go + -ing, then retell them with went + -ing and have gone + -ing.

exercises.prompt: The organiser has confirmed that the event is cancelled. There is ___ waiting outside the venue.
exercises.feedback: No point in + -ing expresses that waiting cannot improve the outcome after the cancellation.

exercises.prompt: The temporary art display closes tomorrow. It is ___ before the paintings leave town.
exercises.feedback: Use worth + -ing to recommend an experience that justifies the effort.

exercises.prompt: Although she was new to the system, Noor had no trouble ___ the figures.
exercises.feedback: Have no trouble + -ing reports that an activity was easy to complete.

exercises.prompt: After their final exams, the classmates went ___ on the river.
exercises.feedback: The leisure-activity pattern is went + -ing: went kayaking.

exercises.prompt: The decision is final, so there is no point ___ with the referee. (argue; include the required preposition)
acceptedAnswers: in arguing
exercises.feedback: No point is followed by in + -ing to describe a futile action.

exercises.prompt: The detailed guide is ___ before you start the repair. (worth / read)
acceptedAnswers: worth reading
exercises.feedback: Worth is followed by the -ing form reading.

exercises.prompt: The audience had difficulty ___ the speaker from the back row. (hear; write only its -ing form)
acceptedAnswers: hearing
exercises.feedback: The difficulty pattern takes hearing directly; this gap asks for the -ing verb alone.

exercises.prompt: I spent most of the afternoon ___ the receipts. (organise; use British spelling and the -ing form)
acceptedAnswers: organising
exercises.feedback: Spend time + -ing describes how the afternoon was used; British spelling is organising.

exercises.prompt: Correct only the verb pattern after worth: The live performance is worth to watch if you enjoy jazz.
acceptedAnswers: The live performance is worth watching if you enjoy jazz.
exercises.feedback: Worth requires watching, not to watch.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: It is no good to complaining when the shop is already closed.
acceptedAnswers: It is no good complaining when the shop is already closed.
exercises.feedback: No good goes directly before the -ing form complaining, without to.

exercises.prompt: Correct only the verb pattern after difficulty: The team had difficulty to access the archive.
acceptedAnswers: The team had difficulty accessing the archive.
exercises.feedback: Have difficulty takes -ing, so use accessing instead of to access.

exercises.prompt: Correct only the extra preposition: We went to hiking in the hills last weekend.
acceptedAnswers: We went hiking in the hills last weekend.
exercises.feedback: Go hiking is the normal activity expression; remove to.

speakingExercises.prompt: The reception desk is closed for the entire day. Say one sentence beginning “There is no point in” and ending “again” about calling the desk.
acceptedAnswers: There is no point in calling the reception desk again.
There's no point in calling the reception desk again.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use there is no point in + calling because another attempt will not help.

speakingExercises.prompt: Recommend a guided walk using these exact words: the guided walk / be / worth / take. Say one complete present-tense sentence.
acceptedAnswers: The guided walk is worth taking.

speakingExercises.prompt: Maya struggled to connect the projector. Describe this past difficulty with “Maya had difficulty” and end with “the projector”.
acceptedAnswers: Maya had difficulty connecting the projector.
speakingExercises.feedback: Had difficulty + connecting names the action she struggled with.

speakingExercises.prompt: State how the team used its time yesterday: the team / spend two hours / rehearse the presentation / yesterday. Use spent + -ing.
acceptedAnswers: The team spent two hours rehearsing the presentation yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Spent + a time expression + rehearsing is the natural pattern.

speakingExercises.prompt: A colleague asks why the decorators cannot come to lunch. Given fact: they are preparing the hall this afternoon. Begin with “They are busy” and end with “this afternoon”.
acceptedAnswers: They are busy preparing the hall this afternoon.
They're busy preparing the hall this afternoon.
speakingExercises.feedback: Be busy + preparing names the activity preventing them from joining lunch.

speakingExercises.prompt: You cannot provide the forgotten password. Say one sentence starting with “It is no good” and ending with “the password” using ask me about.
acceptedAnswers: It is no good asking me about the password.
It's no good asking me about the password.
speakingExercises.feedback: No good is followed directly by asking, without to.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make exactly two sentences. Fact one: the match is cancelled, so waiting will not help; start with “There is no point in” and end with “the match”. Fact two: your group will go climbing instead; start with “We will”.
acceptedAnswers: There is no point in waiting for the match. We will go climbing instead.
There's no point in waiting for the match. We will go climbing instead.
There is no point in waiting for the match. We'll go climbing instead.
There's no point in waiting for the match. We'll go climbing instead.
speakingExercises.feedback: The first sentence uses no point in + -ing, while the second uses go climbing.

speakingExercises.prompt: Report a completed leisure outing in one sentence. Use these exact facts: the neighbours / go camping / by the lake / last Saturday. Use the past simple.
acceptedAnswers: The neighbours went camping by the lake last Saturday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Went camping is the natural past-tense activity expression.

listeningExercises.audioText: We tried calling the organiser twice, but the festival has been cancelled. There is no point in trying again.
listeningExercises.prompt: What does the speaker think about trying to contact the organiser again?
listeningExercises.feedback: The cancellation makes another attempt unhelpful, so the speaker uses no point in trying again.

listeningExercises.audioText: The guided tour costs a little more, but the stories behind the artwork make it worth paying for.
listeningExercises.prompt: Why does the speaker think the guided tour is worth its price?
choices: It ends earlier than other tours.
listeningExercises.feedback: The additional stories make the extra cost worthwhile.

listeningExercises.audioText: Our team had trouble installing the new software during the workshop.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word phrase immediately after “had”.
acceptedAnswers: trouble installing
listeningExercises.feedback: Had trouble installing expresses difficulty performing the action.

listeningExercises.audioText: Mira spent nearly all morning editing the promotional video and still missed the deadline.
listeningExercises.prompt: What occupied most of Mira’s morning?
listeningExercises.feedback: Spent nearly all morning editing identifies the activity that consumed her time.

listeningExercises.audioText: Theo is too busy preparing the costumes to answer any messages right now.
listeningExercises.prompt: Why is Theo not answering his messages?
listeningExercises.feedback: Busy preparing the costumes explains why messages must wait.

listeningExercises.audioText: Every summer, our neighbours go paddleboarding on the lake, not kayaking.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which activity do the neighbours usually do at the lake?
listeningExercises.feedback: The speaker contrasts go paddleboarding with kayaking to identify the usual activity.

listeningExercises.audioText: It is no good debating the price with a machine that cannot change it.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three words immediately after “It is”.
acceptedAnswers: no good debating
listeningExercises.feedback: It is no good + -ing expresses that the proposed discussion cannot help.

listeningExercises.audioText: That documentary is worth watching even if you already know the history.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word phrase immediately after “is”.
acceptedAnswers: worth watching
listeningExercises.feedback: Worth watching recommends the documentary as a rewarding use of time.
